title: California's 15th Congressional District General Election, 2026
description: This race will decide the U.S. House representative for California's 15th Congressional District, which covers most of San Mateo County in the San Francisco Bay Area. Incumbent Democrat Kevin Mullin, first elected in 2022, faces Republican challenger Charles Hoelter, a retired UPS supervisor and first-time candidate. The district is heavily Democratic (D+26 Cook Partisan Voting Index) and rated 'Solid D' by the Cook Political Report, giving Mullin a strong advantage heading into the general election. California's top-two primary was held June 2, 2026, with Mullin receiving 65.0% and Hoelter 18.7% of the vote, advancing over three other candidates.
polling_note: No general election opinion polls were found for this race as of the research date. The Cook Political Report rates the district as 'Solid D' based on its D+26 Partisan Voting Index.

candidates.name: Kevin Mullin
candidates.summary: Kevin Mullin is the incumbent U.S. Representative for California's 15th Congressional District, first elected in 2022. Prior to Congress, he served in the California State Assembly from 2012 to 2022, including eight years as Speaker pro Tempore, and previously served on the South San Francisco City Council including one term as mayor. Mullin has focused on climate resilience, democracy reform, and affordable housing, and was one of the architects of a $3.7 billion climate resilience package that funded Caltrain electrification.

candidates.name: Charles Hoelter
candidates.summary: Charles Hoelter is a Republican candidate for U.S. House in California's 15th Congressional District and the sole Republican to advance from the top-two primary. He is a retired UPS supervisor who has lived in San Mateo County for over three decades. His campaign focuses on conservative priorities including term limits, voter ID requirements, keeping men out of women's sports, apprenticeship programs, secure borders, and support for law enforcement.

forecast.rationale: No general-election polling exists, which limits certainty and keeps confidence at medium. However, all other indicators point to an overwhelming Democratic advantage: the district has a D+26 Cook Partisan Voting Index and is rated 'Solid D' by Cook Political Report. Incumbent Democrat Kevin Mullin (first elected 2022) dominated the June 2, 2026 top-two primary with 65.0% of the vote, while Republican challenger Charles Hoelter—a retired UPS supervisor and first-time candidate—received only 18.7%. The district covers most of San Mateo County in the San Francisco Bay Area, a consistently deep-blue region. District partisanship, incumbency, candidate experience disparity, and the primary vote share all converge to indicate a near-certain Democratic hold.
